- A contact for on-call infra during the demo in case we see backpressure.

Thanks,
Anna

On Mon, Mar 22, 2027 at 09:35, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — forwarding Velotech's ask. Key points: April 5th demo, ~900 rpm short bursts, 350–450 sustained.

We can do a targeted, time-bound per-customer throttle override on Hosted. Implementation notes / constraints:
- Needs an explicit API key + allowlist for that key so override doesn't leak to others.
- We'll gate the waiver behind an internal feature flag and a release that can be toggled quickly.
- Risk: if traffic patterns exceed their profile for >10 minutes at the 900 rpm level, backend queuing will increase P95 latency. We'll want dynamic retry/backoff guidance for their SDK.

Operational ask from our side:
1) We need the exact API key they'll use and the UTC window (we should include a 5-minute buffer before/after).
2) Velotech should send a 30-second canary blast 48 hours before the demo to the same key so we can validate routing.
3) On-call contact: I'll be primary for the demo window, +1 is Neha Kapoor. I'll post PagerDuty rotation and pair with support for chat ops.

I'll prepare a short runbook (commands to toggle flag, rollback steps, dashboard panels) and attach it to the Drive link.

Dylan

Quick product check on requirements:
- If this is solely a throttle exceptions path (no model variant changes), we can avoid a code-path change. Good.
- We should capture SLA expectations in writing: will Velotech expect 99th percentile latency guarantees during the waiver? I recommend we clearly mark this as "best-effort" for latency and limit any SLA exposure.
- Telemetry: require them to set X-Client-Runbook and include trace-id propagation (we can correlate spans).
- Canary criteria: successful canary = no 429s, P95 token latency increase < 30% vs baseline, CPU/GPU utilization within expected ranges.

I'll draft a short "waiver policy" line to include in the credit / contract addendum. Laura — can you review wording so we avoid any implied SLA lift?
